contracts: Markers are ASCII; argv/env use lowercase UTF-16 JSON escapes; text accepts raw-byte \xHH.
dependencies: crates/omni-fixture implements the verbs; conformance/scenarios and qa consume them.
failures_or_limits: The documented single-write marker claim is stronger than Out::write's write_all implementation guarantees at syscall level.
purpose: Defines the executable fixture language shared by conformance and QA.
behavior: Ordered arguments are fixture steps; unknown verbs or malformed values are declared to print FIXTURE-ERROR and exit 99.
Documents output/stdin, environment, tree/signal resistance, pid logs/watchers, allocation and PTY probes; descendants use the same executable and escapees self-exit after 60 seconds.

evidence.quote:
0. An unknown verb or a bad value prints `FIXTURE-ERROR <reason>` to stderr and exits 99. Text values accept the
escapes `\n \r \t \\ \xHH` (`\xHH` writes a raw byte, so invalid UTF-8 is expressible).

Descendants are the fixture itself (same binary), started without a shell, inheriting stdio unless stated. They run
the internal steps `_level=<k>:<n>[:resist]` (`tree`) and `_escaped` (`escape`); an escaped descendant exits after
60 s, because nothing else ends it. `argv` and `env` print compact JSON in ASCII: non-ASCII characters as `\uXXXX`
(UTF-16, lowercase hex).

contracts: Default OS scope is Linux/macOS/Windows; all languages apply unless listed; each action defaults to 10000 ms.
Listed result fields must match; omitted fields are ignored; processes match unordered one-to-one and pid lists as sets.
dependencies: regex-table.json defines differential patterns; docs/api-contract.md defines mapped option names.
failures_or_limits: Python is declared v0.2; the document does not establish a shipped or executed Python runner.
purpose: Defines the shared JSON scenario language, deadlines and assertion semantics.
behavior: Every applicable scenario is mandatory: skipped scenarios and action timeouts fail; only unrepresentable inputs justify language restrictions.
Ten action families use shared AbortSignal, temporary files/captures, complete-line regex matching and single output ownership.

evidence.quote:
Each step has exactly one action key. The value of the key is the handle name (`as` of an earlier step) or, for
`run`/`spawn`, `[command, ...args]`. Every step fails after 10 s unless it states `timeoutMs`; a timeout is a
failure, never a pass.

`expect` lists fields of the step's result; every listed field must match, and unlisted fields are ignored.
- **Thrown/rejected error:** `error` (code), `message` (substrings that must all appear), `result` (fields of
  `error.result`).

contracts: Release requires an empty active pending list.
dependencies: docs/acceptance.md defines owners; conformance runners classify outcomes using this file.
failures_or_limits: An empty registry is source state, not evidence of a passing suite.
purpose: Provides the lead-owned pending-contract registry and release policy.
behavior: Contains only explanatory comments, with no active pending ID/work-package rows.
A listed expected failure is pending; an unexpectedly passing listed item fails until the lead removes it.

evidence.quote:
# Contract items that cannot pass yet: `<ID> <WP>`, the owner from docs/acceptance.md. Only the lead edits this
# file; it must be empty for a release. A pending item that fails is reported as `pending`; one that passes fails

contracts: Each accepted pattern must satisfy match/nomatch/group1 rows; each refused pattern must fail the subset validator; JS uses the u flag.
dependencies: conformance/SPEC.md defines the portable regex subset; Rust regex and JS RegExp consume the table.
failures_or_limits: Finite fixtures do not establish equivalence for every possible expression/input.
purpose: Specifies accepted/refused regex cases shared by Rust and JavaScript runners.
behavior: Accepted examples cover ASCII digit/word classes, Unicode and astral code points, escaping, quantifiers and group-one extraction.
Refused examples include lookarounds, backreferences, named groups, flags, Unicode properties, whitespace/boundary shorthand and malformed/repeated quantifiers.

evidence.quote: "about": "Differential table of the scenario regex subset (conformance/SPEC.md). Every runner compiles each accepted pattern with its own engine (JavaScript: new RegExp(p, \"u\"), matching by code point) and checks it: each `match` input matches, no `nomatch` input matches, and `group1` maps an input to the text of group 1. Every `refused` pattern must be refused by the runner's subset check.",

contracts: No shell is invoked; descendants remain external test actors.
dependencies: main.rs executes internal steps; out.rs writes escape result markers.
failures_or_limits: Windows refusal marker conflates spawn failure causes; dropped Child handles do not join descendants.
purpose: Starts same-executable fixture descendants with inherited stdio and pid logging.
behavior: current_exe commands prepend active pidlog; tree levels recurse through _level; hold and alloc-child null stdin.
Unix escape starts _escaped; Windows tries CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB and prints ESCAPE-REFUSED for any spawn error; escapees live 60 seconds.
copy_self creates destination parents and copies the current executable.

evidence.quote: pub const ESCAPEE_LIFETIME: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);

contracts: READY/PID/GOT/LOGGED/SIZE are synchronization markers; alloc touches 4096-byte pages and retains memory.
dependencies: parse.rs validates; descend.rs creates processes; sys handles OS effects; out.rs writes/formats.
failures_or_limits: watch treats read errors as empty content and has no internal deadline; the caller must bound it. Allocation/input counting can grow without product limits.
purpose: Executes the fixture DSL and emits observable process behavior for assertions.
behavior: All arguments parse before run; failures produce FIXTURE-ERROR/99; explicit exit preserves full Windows u32 and Unix low-eight-bit behavior.
Implements raw output, stdin echo/count, argv/env, line handshakes, descendants, pid logs, allocation and terminal probes.
Watch polls complete log lines every 5 ms; sizes uses a stdin-reader thread and emits changed dimensions.

contracts: Out routes stdout/stderr; all sink writes use write_all.
dependencies: main.rs and descend.rs send markers/data through Out.
failures_or_limits: write_all may issue multiple syscalls despite the module's single-write comment; handle duplication failure falls back silently.
purpose: Writes deterministic fixture bytes and ASCII-only JSON strings.
behavior: Duplicates standard handles when possible; Windows terminals use standard console streams for UTF-8 conversion.
Alphabet patterns use 65520-byte blocks; lines/repeats batch around 60000 bytes; JSON emits non-ASCII as lowercase UTF-16 escapes.
Write failure prints FIXTURE-ERROR and exits 99; standard stdout fallback flushes.

contracts: Streams must be stdout/stderr; numeric types enforce representation, not workload resource caps.
dependencies: sys supplies signal_number; out supplies Stream; main consumes Step.
failures_or_limits: Large allocation/watch counts remain expressible; argv intentionally bypasses step Unicode parsing.
purpose: Parses and validates every fixture argument into typed steps before execution.
behavior: argv consumes remaining OsStrings verbatim; other arguments require valid Unicode and split at the first equals.
Parses stream/count triples, resistant tree levels, unsigned numbers, paths and OS-valid signals; unknown verbs and malformed values return diagnostic strings.
Text supports newline, CR, tab, backslash and raw hex escapes; bare verbs reject values and :resist must be a complete suffix.

contracts: The module declares unsafe fixture OS operations belong under sys.
dependencies: sys/unix.rs and sys/windows.rs implement effects; main.rs emits tty JSON.
failures_or_limits: Out-of-range selectors implicitly mean stderr rather than producing an error.
purpose: Selects platform fixture syscall helpers and terminal detection.
behavior: cfg(unix)/cfg(windows) expose their respective helper modules.
is_tty maps 0 to stdin, 1 to stdout and every other selector to stderr.

contracts: Unsafe operations include SAFETY explanations; farewell records are never freed.
dependencies: libc supplies POSIX APIs; main.rs invokes these effects in test actors.
failures_or_limits: Signal registration, setsid and close results are not propagated; repeated on_term registration intentionally leaks records.
purpose: Implements Unix fixture signal behavior, session escape, stdin closure and terminal size.
behavior: raise restores default disposition and unblocks a recognized terminating signal; ignore/default/on-term affect SIGTERM and SIGHUP.
on_term atomically publishes leaked immutable farewell data and the handler calls write/_exit.
setsid attempts escape, close_stdin closes fd 0 and terminal size probes stdout/stdin/stderr before returning 0x0.

contracts: Handlers use Windows system ABI and on_term text initializes once.
dependencies: windows-sys Console/Foundation APIs are enabled by the crate manifest; main.rs invokes the helper surface.
failures_or_limits: Registration/close failures are not surfaced; repeated on_term retains the first text; resistant close handlers require external forced cleanup.
purpose: Implements Windows fixture console-control handlers and terminal probes.
behavior: Signal names are unsupported; setsid and default_term are no-ops because console handlers are not inherited.
ignore_term handles Ctrl-C/Break and blocks indefinitely for close-or-later events; on_term uses OnceLock text and exits 0 for C/Break/Close.
Closes the standard input handle and reads visible console window dimensions, falling back to 0x0.
